history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is at Chitai village, ~8-9 km from Almora town on the Jageshwar road (SH-37), not in Almora itself; documented with the corrected location. Chitai Golu Devta is the most famous of the many Golu Devta shrines of Kumaon, the 'temple of a million bells'. Golu Devta is venerated as an incarnation of Lord Shiva as Gaur Bhairav and as the God of Justice: devotees write their grievances on stamped paper or letters and hang them on the temple walls, and tie a brass bell when a wish is fulfilled - thousands of bells hang all over the complex. One tradition dates the shrine to the 12th century, built by a commander of the Chand dynasty that ruled Almora; folklore links Golu to the Rai dynasty of Dhumakot (c. 15th century). Another account (optimatravels) says Golu Devta was a general of Chand king Baj Bahadur (1638-1678) who died in battle and was enshrined here. The shrine sits amid dense chir-pine forest and is the most sacred temple for the people of Almora and the neighbouring villages.

name: Chitai Golu Devta Temple
town: Chitai (CSV town 'Almora' is imprecise - the temple is ~8-9 km from Almora town on the Almora-Jageshwar road)
town_description: Chitai is a small village on State Highway 37 between Almora and Jageshwar in the Kumaon Himalaya, set amid dense chir-pine and mimosa forest. Its fame rests entirely on the bell temple of Golu Devta, one of the most visited religious sites around Almora.
